## Loading Data

```{r}
#| label: load-data-ms2022
#| warning: false

ms2022 <- read_excel("data/DSA 406 Annual Data 2022.xlsx")
ms2022 <- ms2022 |>
  filter(!is.na(restaurant))

glimpse(ms2022)
```

[MenuStat](https://www.menustat.org/faq.html) is a free nutrition database that aggregates menu and nutrition information from major U.S. chain restaurants, allowing users to compare food items across restaurants and analyze changes in nutritional content over time.

To learn more about the dataset and its variables, review the [Menu Stat Datasheet](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1rDKTth3tAOar71xh-GWEhU4mRa9A7aF8_CdiNyqFWdo/edit?tab=t.bxwvivhu4jol).

```{r}
#| label: view-head

head(ms2022)
```

**Question 1.** Find the 10 restaurants with the fewest menu items in the dataset.

```{r}
#| label: menu-items

# Count how many menu items each restaurant has, sort from most
# to fewest, then keep the last 10 rows (the 10 restaurants with
# the fewest menu items).
restaurants <- ms2022 |>
  count(restaurant) |>
  arrange(desc(n)) |>
  tail(10)

restaurants
```

**Question 2.** Compute summary statistics for the `calories` variable.

```{r}
#| label: cal-summary

# Basic summary statistics (min, quartiles, mean, max) for calories
summary(ms2022$calories)
```

**Question 3.** Create a histogram showing the distribution of calories for all menu items across restaurants. Mark the maximum calorie value on the histogram.

```{r}
#| label: cal-distribution
#| fig-cap: "Calorie distribution of all menu items across restaurants."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

# Find the highest calorie value, and create histogram
max_calories <- max(ms2022$calories, na.rm = TRUE)

ggplot(ms2022, aes(x = calories)) +
  geom_histogram() +
  geom_point(aes(x = max_calories, y = 0), color = "red") +
  labs(x = "Calories", y = "Frequency") +
  theme_classic()
```

**Question 4.** Find the menu item with the highest number of calories.

```{r}
#| label: highest-cal-item


ms2022 |>
  filter(calories == max(calories, na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  select(restaurant, item_name, item_description, calories)
```

**Question 5.** Find the highest-calorie menu item for each restaurant identified in **Question 1**.

```{r}
#| label: highest-cal-item-restaurant

highest_cal_restaurant <- ms2022 |>
  filter(restaurant %in% restaurants$restaurant) |>
  group_by(restaurant) |>
  slice_max(calories, n = 1) |>
  select(restaurant, item_name, calories) |>
  arrange(desc(calories))

highest_cal_restaurant
```

**Question 6.** Create a bar chart showing the highest-calorie menu item for each restaurant identified in **Question 1**.

```{r}
#| label: fig-highest-cal-restaurant
#| fig-cap: "Highest-calorie menu item for selected restaurants."



ggplot(highest_cal_restaurant, aes(x = reorder(restaurant, calories), y = calories)) +
  geom_col() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Calories") +
  theme_classic()
```

**Question 7.** Create a boxplot showing the calorie distribution for menu items from the top five restaurants identified in **Question 1**.

```{r}
#| label: fig-cal-dist-restaurant
#| fig-cap: "Calorie distribution of menu items for selected restaurants."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

ms2022 |>
  filter(restaurant %in% restaurants$restaurant[1:5]) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = restaurant, y = calories)) +
  geom_boxplot() +
  labs(x = "", y = "Calories") +
  theme_classic()
```

**Question 8.** Identify and inspect invalid or non-numeric values in the `sodium` variable.

```{r}
#| label: err-sodium

err_sodium <- ms2022 |>
  filter(!grepl("^-?\\d*\\.?\\d+$", sodium))

unique(err_sodium$sodium)
table(err_sodium$sodium, useNA = "ifany")
```

**Question 9.** Clean and summarize the `sodium` variable by keeping only numeric values.

```{r}
#| label: clean-sodium

clean_sodium <- ms2022 |>
  filter(grepl("^-?\\d*\\.?\\d+$", sodium)) |>
  pull(sodium) |>
  as.numeric()

summary(clean_sodium)
```

**Question 10.** Clean and summarize the `sodium` variable by keeping only numeric values. Then create a boxplot showing the calorie distribution for menu items from the top five restaurants identified in **Question 1**.

```{r}
#| label: fig-sodium-dist-restaurant
#| fig-cap: "Sodium distribution of menu items for selected restaurants."
#| message: false
#| warning: false

ms2022 |>
  filter(grepl("^-?\\d*\\.?\\d+$", sodium), 
         restaurant %in% restaurants$restaurant[1:5]) |>
  mutate(clean_sodium_col = as.numeric(sodium)) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = restaurant, y = clean_sodium_col)) +
  geom_boxplot() + 
  labs(x = "", y = "Sodium") +
  theme_classic()
```
